root_cause.text: The `ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents` function incorrectly passes the `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` flag when calling `ext4_split_convert_extents` to split an unwritten extent before submitting I/O, which causes the entire on-disk extent to be marked as written if the split fails due to `-ENOSPC`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the removal of `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` from the flags passed to `ext4_split_convert_extents` in `ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents`, and the CVE description explains that this flag causes `ext4_split_extent_at` to convert the entire on-disk extent to written when a split fails due to a temporary `-ENOSPC`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix extent splitting by ensuring the second split extent is only marked valid when converting to initialized.
intent_record.what: Modified the condition in ext4_split_convert_extents to handle EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_UNWRIT_EXT, and made the assignment of EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 to split_flag conditional on EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when splitting an unwritten extent without converting it, the second part of the split extent is not incorrectly marked as containing valid initialized data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid incorrectly passing the EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT flag when splitting unwritten extents with the nomerge flag set.
intent_record.what: Modified the call to ext4_split_convert_extents within ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents to pass the flags parameter directly instead of bitwise-ORing it with EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT.
intent_record.how: Prevents the EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT flag from being incorrectly set when splitting unwritten extents under the EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_SPLIT_NOMERGE condition, ensuring correct extent state preservation.
